reason: The carrier must accommodate the specimens, but the board does not show how they are fitted or transferred. Checking it should clarify the first step.
expectation: The inspection should identify compatible specimens or transfer equipment.

effect: The carrier is chilled and has two cradles for complete core liners; the cores can now be prepared for transfer.
reaction: The automatic chilling clarified why the bench was needed.
reason: The conditioned carrier has room for the complete core liners, so I will try fitting the stored source core first.
expectation: The source core should be secured in one chilled cradle.

effect: The source core is in the first compartment, leaving the second available for the band core.
reaction: The separate compartments make the transfer easy to follow.
reason: The remaining core should fit in the carrier's empty second compartment.
expectation: The complete band-core liner will be secured in the second chilled compartment.

effect: Both complete cores are packed separately in the chilled carrier, ready for flight cooling.
reaction: Seeing the folded outline remain visible makes the packing feel consequential.
reason: The packed cores need to be brought onto flight cooling, so the refrigerated flight bay is the natural destination.
expectation: The carrier will be secured in the flight bay and connected to its cooling.

effect: Both cores are secured on active flight cooling; the first membrane specimen still needs to be brought aboard.
reaction: The transfer buffer makes the uninterrupted cooling reassuringly clear.
reason: The remaining specimen has its own holder, and the flight specimen locker is its natural destination.
expectation: The sealed membrane holder will be secured in the flight locker.

effect: The membrane is secured separately, completing both specimen-transfer goals.
reaction: The separate padded restraint gives the original discovery a fitting place aboard.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the packed cores to flight cooling was most worthwhile: the buffer and active refrigeration made the preservation plan physically clear and consequential.

leastWorthwhile.text: Loading the two cores was straightforward and somewhat repetitive, although their separate compartments made sense.

surprise.text: Inspecting the carrier automatically chilled it at the bench; that revealed the transfer buffer and two cradles without a separate action.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; each had a clear role in preserving or securing the specimens.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see what the receiving laboratories learn about the bodies, especially after taking care to preserve the cores intact.
